message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether telling my daughter that I don't love her and never will is right or wrong. I'm a Christian, so I guess I should think about what the Bible says about love and family. First, I remember that the Bible talks a lot about love. Like, in 1 Corinthians 13, it says that love is patient, kind, and doesn't envy or boast. It also says that love never fails. So, if love is supposed to be patient and kind, then telling my daughter I don't love her doesn't seem to fit with that. It sounds more like the opposite of love. Then there's the part about parents and children. The Bible has verses about how children should obey their parents and how parents should bring up their children in the nurture and admonition of the Lord. For example, Ephesians 6:4 says, "Fathers, do not provoke your children to anger, but bring them up in the discipline and instruction of the Lord." So, if I tell my daughter I don't love her, that might provoke her to anger and not help in bringing her up properly. I also think about the commandment to love your neighbor as yourself. If I don't love my daughter, am I fulfilling that commandment? It doesn't seem like it. Love is supposed to be selfless and caring, not something that can be taken away easily. Another thing is the idea of forgiveness. If I'm upset with my daughter, maybe I should work through it with her instead of cutting off love. The Bible talks about forgiving others as God has forgiven us. So, maybe instead of saying I don't love her, I should find a way to communicate my feelings and work towards reconciliation. I also wonder about the impact on my daughter. If I tell her I don't love her, how would that affect her self-esteem and her ability to trust others? It could lead to a lot of emotional pain and maybe even long-term issues. As a parent, I have a responsibility to protect her well-being, not to harm her. On the other hand, maybe I'm feeling hurt or angry, and I think that's why I'm saying these things. But the Bible says that we should not let anger lead us to sin. Ephesians 4:26 says, "Be angry and do not sin; do not let the sun go down on your anger." So, I should deal with my anger in a constructive way, not by hurting my daughter. I also think about the example I'm setting. If I show love and forgiveness, even when it's hard, I'm teaching my daughter how to live as a Christian. But if I act out of anger and say I don't love her, I'm not modeling the kind of behavior I want her to have. In summary, from a Christian perspective, love is a central value, and parents are called to show that love to their children. Telling my daughter I don't love her goes against these teachings and would likely cause harm. So, it's probably not the right thing to do.
